Container.Name: Cellarly
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted wine cellar manager. Every bottle lives at an exact row and position in a rack you can spin around in 3D, on a server that is entirely yours.
Cellarly is in beta: every release so far is a pre-release of 1.0.0. This template runs the beta tag, the newest release.
Search a wine catalog or snap a photo of the label, track what you paid and what it is worth, rate what you drink and watch the drink-window countdown. Everyone in your household gets an account with a cellar of their own, in German or English.
Sign in as the admin with the email and password you set below. Everyone else registers at /register, and you approve them on the Admin page; set Registration open to false to take no more. No mail server is needed.
Everything is stored in one SQLite file in the data folder, backed up daily and before an upgrade changes it, and downloadable and restorable from the Admin page. Keep that folder on a disk or pool of this server, not on a network share (NFS or SMB), where SQLite does not work reliably. Google Gemini (optional API key) powers label recognition, enrichment and the price and critics lookup.
Free software under the AGPL-3.0. Source code: https://gitlab.com/coderoftime/cellarly, and Settings links to the source of the version you run.
Container.Changes:
1.0.0-beta.7 (2026-11-10) - A sign-in ends after 30 days without use (Session idle days), and everyone signs in once more after this upgrade. - Registration open set to false takes no more registrations. The admin's account button shows how many are waiting. - Type a drinking window by hand. "Enhance with AI" only fills empty fields, which Save keeps and Cancel drops. - Countries in your language, messages that say why a sign-in or Gemini failed, and keyboard and screen-reader fixes. - The Docker page shows the container as healthy. An admin that an empty Admin email left without an address gets one on the next start: the address set, or admin@localhost. - Upgrading: a cleared Secure cookie field now keeps the cookie Secure; set it to false to sign in over http:// from another device. - Upgrading: clear Trusted proxies if it says 172.17.0.0/16. To count visitors behind a proxy, put the proxy and Cellarly on a custom network with a fixed IP for the proxy, list that IP, and point the proxy at Cellarly by its container name (Behind a reverse proxy in Cellarly's README). - Upgrading: over plain http://, a proxy that does not pass the Host header on as the browser sent it, port included, such as Nginx Proxy Manager on a port other than 80, gets every sign-in refused until it is set up as that page says. - Upgrading: reset mail goes only over TLS or STARTTLS unless SMTP allow plaintext is true, and SMTP secure true now means TLS from the first byte, so use it with port 465, not 587.
1.0.0-beta.6 (2026-11-05) - Backups on the Admin page: download the database, or restore one. - A daily backup into the data folder, keeping the newest 14. - Export your bottles, wishlist, ratings and history as CSV from Settings. - Readable label on the red confirm buttons.
1.0.0-beta.5 (2026-11-04) - "Look up price & ratings" now answers in 10 to 25 seconds instead of timing out.
1.0.0-beta.4 (2026-11-04) - Look up a wine's market price and critic scores (needs a paid Gemini key). - An estimated cellar worth in Statistics.
Full history: https://gitlab.com/coderoftime/cellarly/-/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the web interface is served on.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The SQLite database and its automatic backups. This is the only state the app has. Keep it on a disk or pool of this server, not on a network share (NFS or SMB), where SQLite does not work reliably.

Config.Name: Session secret
Config.Description: Signs and encrypts the session cookie. At least 32 random characters, e.g. from `openssl rand -base64 32`. With a shorter one, or none, Cellarly does not start, and the log says so. Keep it stable: changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: Admin password
Config.Description: Password of the admin account, which the first start creates. At least 8 characters, and not choose-a-password, the example an earlier Cellarly README showed: otherwise there is no admin, registering stays closed, and the log says why. Changing it here later has no effect; change it in Cellarly under Change password in the account menu.

Config.Name: Admin email
Config.Description: Email the admin signs in with, read when the first start creates the admin; changing it later has no effect, except that an admin an earlier Cellarly created with no address, because this field was empty, gets it on the next start. It has to be an address no account has yet: otherwise no admin is created, and the log says so. Empty means admin@localhost.

Config.Name: Registration open
Config.Description: true or empty: anyone who can reach Cellarly can ask for an account at /register, and the admin approves it or not. false takes no more registrations: the sign-in page no longer links to /register, which says it is closed. Any other value closes it too.

Config.Name: Secure cookie
Config.Description: false lets a browser keep the sign-in over plain http://, as when you open Cellarly at http://your-server:3000 from another device. Anything else, empty included, keeps the cookie Secure, which a browser keeps only over HTTPS: over http:// the sign-in page then says the browser did not keep the sign-in. Set it to true once Cellarly is reached only over HTTPS.

Config.Name: Gemini API key
Config.Description: Optional. Google Gemini key for label photos, enrichment, catalog search beyond the wines already in Cellarly, and the price and critics lookup. Without it, search answers from the catalog alone, and the camera, Enhance with AI and the lookup are not offered. Enhance with AI and the lookup search with Google Search, which needs a paid key.

Config.Name: Session idle days
Config.Description: How many days a sign-in lasts without being used. Each use starts them again, so whoever uses Cellarly stays signed in. Fractions such as 0.5 work. Empty means 30.

Config.Name: Daily backups kept
Config.Description: How many daily backups of the database to keep in the backups folder. Empty means 14, 0 switches them off. Backups taken before an upgrade or a restore are never deleted.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Your reverse proxy's own address, or several, comma-separated, so the sign-in limits count each visitor rather than the proxy. Put the proxy, such as Nginx Proxy Manager, and Cellarly on a custom Docker network where the proxy has a fixed IP, list that IP, and its IPv6 address too if the network has IPv6, and point the proxy at Cellarly by its container name and port 3000, not at this server's address. Never list a network's gateway (x.x.x.1, such as 172.17.0.1) or a range that includes it, such as 172.17.0.0/16: IPv6 visitors, and connections from the server itself or from a container to the server's address, reach Cellarly from the gateway, and whoever connects from a listed address can claim any address. See Behind a reverse proxy in Cellarly's README.

Config.Name: SMTP host
Config.Description: Optional. Together with SMTP from and SMTP public URL it switches on password-reset mails; without them an admin issues a temporary password instead. The mail goes out encrypted, see SMTP secure.

Config.Name: SMTP from
Config.Description: Sender address of the password-reset mail, e.g. cellar@example.com.

Config.Name: SMTP public URL
Config.Description: Address the reset link points to, e.g. https://cellarly.example.com

Config.Name: SMTP port
Config.Description: Empty means 587, or 465 when SMTP secure is true. Set it only for a relay on another port.

Config.Name: SMTP secure
Config.Description: true: TLS from the first byte, on port 465 unless SMTP port names another. false: the connection starts in plain text and switches to TLS with STARTTLS, which the relay has to offer, or it gets no mail unless SMTP allow plaintext is true. Empty: true on port 465, false on any other. Don't set true with port 587 or 25, which start in plain text.

Config.Name: SMTP allow plaintext
Config.Description: Only for a relay with no TLS at all, on this server or a network you trust: true sends the reset mail, and the relay login if there is one, to it unencrypted. Empty or false: a relay that offers neither TLS nor STARTTLS gets no mail.

Config.Name: SMTP user
Config.Description: Only for relays that ask for a login.

Config.Name: SMTP password
Config.Description: Only for relays that ask for a login.
